audit.whatIsWrong: My chart gave Zac the two item stages (Zac / Zac / Zac / Zac / Skill / Zac / Zac). The already-audited mirror at audits/top/zac__kassadin.json moved those same two cells to Kassadin.
audit.why: Reusing the mirror rather than re-deciding it. Zac's own page argues that Kassadin outscales — its late text reads 'Kassadin outscales the game late, so the lane was always about ending early' — and it wins only 47.52% over 141 games from Zac's side. My page says the same thing in spikes[3] and whys[6]. Both directions now read Zac / Zac / Zac / Zac / Skill / Kassadin / Kassadin, and the existing ratings already invert correctly (my 6/10 against Zac's 4/10 at both item stages), so no rating change is needed.
audit.corrected: First item and two-plus items are Kassadin, matching the mirror.

audit.whatIsWrong: Cell Division appears nowhere on the page, and whys[6] and spikes[3] both assert flatly that 'Zac is a tank with no late scaling to reclaim'.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Upon taking fatal damage, Zac splits into 4 bloblets that attempt to recombine. If any bloblets remain, he will revive with an amount of Health depending on the Health of the surviving bloblets... This ability has a 5 minute cooldown.' For a champion whose entire win condition is 'blink in, delete one target, blink out', an enemy who comes back from the kill is the most important fact on the page, and it is absent from both layers. The five-minute cooldown also makes it schedulable — it is the longest number in the matchup, and a Zac who already used it is genuinely the tank with nothing left that the page describes.
audit.corrected: Cell Division revives him from four surviving bloblets on a 5-minute cooldown. Clear the blobs or the kill does not count.

audit.whatIsWrong: The itemisation plan is Catalyst into Rod of Ages 'to out-sustain his poke', with no mention that Unstable Matter scales off your maximum health.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Zac explodes outward towards nearby enemies, dealing a percentage of their maximum health as magic damage', 5 second cooldown. Every point of health the Rod of Ages plan adds is more damage taken from a spell he casts every five seconds. That does not make the item wrong — the health still buys you the survival window the lane needs — but the page presents HP as pure mitigation when it is partly a subsidy, and the flagged resistances-invalidated interaction is exactly this. The consolation is that it IS magic damage, so Void Stone and the Null Sphere shield both bite into it, which is the one place the page's Void Stone framing is genuinely earned.
audit.corrected: Unstable Matter takes a percentage of your MAX health every 5 seconds, so Rod of Ages health partly feeds it — the offset is that it is magic, so Void Stone and the Q shield both apply.
sources: champ-data/_kits/zac.json (W description, cooldown 5, range 350, percentHealth flag)

audit.whatIsWrong: Three strings tell you to 'interrupt the charge' of Elastic Slingshot, and none of them gives its cooldown.
audit.why: Kassadin has exactly one interrupt — Null Sphere, which 'interrupts channels' — and nothing in the kit files establishes that a charging Elastic Slingshot counts as a channel; Zac's kit carries no channel flag. The mirror audit reached the same conclusion and deliberately left the interaction out of Zac's page rather than guess. Mine asserts it three times, which is worse: it promises a Kassadin the one defensive answer he does not have. The verifiable replacement is better advice anyway — Elastic Slingshot is 21/18/15/12/9 seconds, so at rank 1 a whiffed sling is a twenty-one-second window, and Stretching Strikes reaches 800 units on 14 seconds while Let's Bounce is 120.
audit.corrected: Elastic Slingshot is 21s at rank 1 — play the window, not an interrupt you may not have. Stretching Strikes is 14s at 800 range; Let's Bounce is 120s.
sources: champ-data/_kits/zac.json (E cooldown 21/18/15/12/9; Q cooldown 14/12.5/11/9.5/8, range 800; R cooldown 120/105/90)
audits/top/zac__kassadin.json (notes: same interaction flagged as unverified from the other side)

audit.why: Recording a trap I did NOT write in: Elastic Slingshot carries a 'grounding' derived flag in Zac's kit file, which would mean it denies Riftwalk and would invert this entire matchup. Riot's description is only 'Zac attaches his arms to the ground and stretches back, launching himself forward' — the flag is a tooltip-parsing artefact of the words 'to the ground'. Treated as a misfire, so the page's core instruction (blink the moment he commits the sling) stands.
sources: champ-data/_kits/zac.json (E description vs its grounding flag)

audit.why: Null Sphere interrupts channels and grants a magic-absorbing shield; it has never silenced in this kit version.
audit.corrected: Null Sphere interrupts channels; it does not silence.

edits.before: This is where the lane flips to me. Through 4-5, Zac is an AP tank, so my passive Void Stone shaves 15% off everything he throws and my Q shield absorbs a chunk of his W blob-burst - his trades just don't hurt the way they should. At 6, Riftwalk is the whole matchup: I blink the instant he commits his E sling and his engage whiffs. Bait the slingshot, dodge it with R, then punish the long cooldown while it's down.
edits.after: This is where the lane flips to you. Through 4-5, Unstable Matter is magic damage, so Void Stone shaves 15% off it and your Q shield absorbs a chunk - but it takes a slice of your MAX health every 5 seconds, so the Rod of Ages you are stacking partly feeds it. At 6, Riftwalk is the whole matchup: blink the instant he commits Elastic Slingshot and the engage whiffs. It is 21s at rank 1 - play that window.

edits.before: Unlike Kayle or Vladimir, Zac is a tank with no scaling spike to reclaim, so the late game is permanently mine. With Riftwalk stacking I blink-kite his slow E sling, blank his magic damage through Void Stone, and Force Pulse comes off cooldown almost instantly in any skirmish where abilities are flying. He is easy to isolate and trades evenly at best - just never get caught flat-footed by his E pin when my R is down, and the 1v9 window is yours.

Cell Division revives him out of four bloblets on a five-minute cooldown, so a kill is not always a kill; clear the blobs or leave. With Riftwalk stacking you blink-kite the slow sling, Void Stone blanks his Unstable Matter, and Force Pulse charges off every spell cast nearby, so it is armed in any real skirmish.

notes: Correction to something the mirror author wrote, because it cost that audit real coverage: audits/top/zac__kassadin.json says 'side values are under the applier's 12-character minimum for a full-layer before and cannot be proposed'. That is a misreading of tools/apply-proposals.js. MIN_LEN_CHECKED is 25 and it EXEMPTS strings shorter than that from the length-drift check rather than blocking them — short values like phases[N].side and phases[N].rating are freely proposable, which is exactly how the whole level chart is meant to be fixed. Zac's page still has phases[5].side and phases[6].side reading 'Zac' while its own content win[] now reads 'Kassadin', so that entry is currently self-contradicting and should be revisited. I have set both layers on my side. Also carried over from the mirror and still unresolved: whether Null Sphere's channel interrupt catches a charging Elastic Slingshot. Neither kit file settles it, so both directions now avoid asserting it and it is in questionsForUser. Last thing, not edited: this page claims 'Zac is an AP tank, so Void Stone shaves 15% off everything he throws', but only Unstable Matter has a stated damage type (magic) in Riot's text — I narrowed the claim to that ability where I rewrote.
